contexts.description: The Next.js App Router root config and authentication/persistence layer. layout.tsx injects Google Fonts and mounts GravitoneTokens as the first body child; app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx provide Next.js error boundary surfaces wired to GlobalErrorBridge so edge errors are surfaced in the studio UI. lib/firebase.ts initializes Firebase Auth with a 12-hour session ceiling; lib/studioDb.ts and lib/projects.ts implement a zero-dependency IndexedDB layer for project CRUD; lib/jobs.tsx is the background-job system for long-running AI tasks; lib/claudeCli.ts spawns a headless local Claude Code process; lib/capabilities.ts exposes a per-deployment feature-flag matrix so surfaces can hide unavailable controls without re-deriving posture from environment keys; lib/deployment.ts answers whether the process can spawn a local binary (the local-first / SaaS split predicate); lib/apiAuth.ts and lib/localMode.ts gate API routes behind auth and local-only flags; lib/identityEviction.ts handles session invalidation; lib/harness/protocol.ts defines the UAT test-automation bridge protocol; lib/announcer.tsx provides screen-reader live-region announcements; lib/formatBrief.ts serialises project briefs for prompt injection.
contexts.name: app-infrastructure

contexts.description: Implements the production asset library across two surfaces and the underlying data layer. The legacy grid (LibraryShelves + AssetsBrowser) provides folder-tree navigation, gallery tiles, right-click/keyboard removal, and a context menu; the new Atelier view is a studio-wall metaphor where visual themes are commissioned works pinned for approval across a brief/preset commission panel, a wall of looks, and a dossier lock flow. The data layer (lib/assets.ts + useAssets, lib/themes.ts + useThemes) stores assets and visual-identity themes as IndexedDB records — assets are pointers (src URLs), themes are four-slot style blocks with approved proof sheets; both are seeded from the trials index and mocked agent-run data.
contexts.name: asset-library

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/foundry/runs, GET /api/foundry/runs/[id], POST /api/foundry/runs/[id]/verdicts, POST /api/foundry/runs/[id]/commit, POST /api/foundry/extract, GET /api/foundry/extract/[id], POST /api/foundry/extract/[id]/step|verdicts|commit, GET /api/foundry/file, GET /api/foundry/styles
contexts.description: The server-side Foundry data layer and API surface — run manifests, style catalogues, verdict persistence, and the Extract engine. lib/foundry/store.ts reads and writes forge-py run manifests from the filesystem; lib/foundry/types.ts defines the full wire type hierarchy (Candidate, Grade, StyleDef, RunManifest, Verdicts, CommitResult); lib/foundry/extract/ is the VLM-backed style extraction engine — engine.ts orchestrates a text/reasoning turn against a gallery's readbacks using lib/text/router.ts, vocabulary.ts defines the closed observable vocabulary, prompts.ts builds the synthesis prompt, and store.ts persists extract runs. The /api/foundry/* routes expose run listing, detail, verdict recording, commit (delete rejected files, write ledger rows), style catalogue, file serving, and the three extract lifecycle endpoints (start, step, verdicts).
contexts.name: foundry-api

contexts.description: The offline Python pipeline that runs for hours on a local GPU rig to produce the raw candidates the /foundry cull page reviews. intake.py ingests source frames from a plan; acquire.py fetches and prepares reference images; forge.py orchestrates the full generation loop (reference annotation → N styles × M mechanisms × seeds of candidates → automatic pre-grade); grade.py runs the VLM grader passes against generated images. plans/ holds sweep configuration JSON files; ledger.json and styles.json are the versioned output indices that the API layer reads. This pipeline owns the write side of the foundry's data; the API layer in lib/foundry/ is the read side.
contexts.name: foundry-pipeline

contexts.description: The /foundry page — where generated style candidates are reviewed and culled by hand before ratification into the style catalogue. FoundryView polls a run manifest and renders two primary surfaces: CullGrid displays a masonry grid of generated candidates with keyboard-driven keep/reject verdicts (immediate, idempotent, debounce-saved); ExtractView and ExtractBoard surface the Extract workflow where a gallery URL is submitted and a VLM turn synthesises named styles with observables and recipes from it. StylesShelf shows the current proven-style catalogue; Lightbox provides a full-screen compare view. foundryClient.ts and extractClient.ts are the typed fetch wrappers for the /api/foundry API.
contexts.name: foundry-ui

contexts.description: Step 3 of the production pipeline — script beats in, composed picture plates out. FramesStep/FramesAssembly render a ledger-style shot list (one row per beat, three layer columns for plate/elements/texts); ShotSheet provides per-beat shot spec editing and shot-level generation control; shots.ts, shotPrompt.ts, and shotReview.ts model the shot entity, build the imaging prompt, and carry the review/approval flow; the alternatives/ sub-directory (AlternativesView, VariantContactSheet, alts.ts, useAlternatives) lets users compare generated variants and pick a winner before locking a frame. frames.ts defines the epistemic three-layer architecture; useFrames orchestrates IndexedDB state and calls /api/frames to derive scene specs via a local Claude CLI run.
contexts.name: frames-step

contexts.description: The golden-path probe test suite — fast, hermetic unit-level specs that verify security invariants, transport resilience, and cross-cutting behavioral contracts without a running server. Each file targets a named seam: imaging SSRF prevention, CLI sandbox argument isolation, CLI transport resilience, object-URL ownership cleanup, imaging/music auth gating, identity persistence, harness-gate wiring, beat-score totals, cut-nudge batching, frames run bounding, style-extraction output, the announcement live-region, music cue briefs and provenance, notebook graph integrity, frames-cut resolution, extract-step lock behaviour, and trailer-cut lifecycle. tests/live/golden-path.live.spec.ts is the integration counterpart that runs the same paths against a real local server.
contexts.name: golden-path-tests

contexts.description: The server-side imaging abstraction layer — three capabilities (generate, edit, recognize) routed across three vendors (Google, Leonardo, Qwen) with zero vendor coupling above lib/imaging/. router.ts reads the environment to pick the right provider per capability; types.ts defines the single ImagingProvider interface all adapters satisfy; lib/stylePrompt.ts is the style-block-to-prompt compiler; pricing.ts is the single source of truth for per-call cost figures; budget.ts enforces per-project spend limits so generation runs cannot exceed a configured ceiling; safeUrl.ts validates image URLs before they are forwarded to any provider, blocking SSRF vectors; log.ts provides structured server logs with credential scrubbing. The three app/api/imaging/* routes are the only seam components may cross.
contexts.name: imaging-providers

contexts.description: The server-side music generation abstraction layer — four capabilities (plan, compose, generate, sfx) routed through ElevenLabs with a thin client facade in lib/musicClient.ts. lib/music/plan.ts turns a scored script into a music brief; lib/music/elevenlabs.ts is the ElevenLabs adapter; lib/music/types.ts defines MusicBrief, MusicTrack, and SfxCue; lib/music/errors.ts provides typed error handling. lib/music/pricing.ts is the single source of truth for per-call cost figures using a three-link unit chain (seconds → credits → USD); lib/music/budget.ts enforces a per-window spend ceiling denominated in seconds of audio requested; lib/music/log.ts writes one structured, credential-scrubbed line per call mirroring the imaging log contract. The five app/api/music/* routes are the only seam components cross — no ElevenLabs import escapes lib/music/.
contexts.name: music-pipeline

contexts.description: The developer-facing pipeline automation layer — driver scripts that exercise the full studio flow headlessly, regression harnesses for gate/bundle/manifest checks, a lint ratchet enforcing code-quality baselines, VLM consistency probe suites, and a knowledge template directory that codifies patterns, open questions, and parameter constraints per studio step. DRIVERS.md documents each script's purpose; drive-research-step.mjs and the other drive-*.mjs files are integration smoke tests run against a live local server; check-bundle.mjs and check-manifest.mjs validate the imaging style bundle manifests; lint-ratchet.mjs enforces that lint errors never exceed the committed baseline. knowledge/templates/trailer/ holds step-level TEMPLATE.md, PATTERNS.md, OPEN-QUESTIONS.md, params.json, and corpus scripts (bar-math.mjs) that ground the generative steps in measurable craft constraints.
contexts.name: pipeline-scripts

contexts.description: The non-script, non-frames production-phase panels (Score, Cut) rendered inside the Studio, plus the shared fixture data that drives all phases at identical proportional scales. ScoreSpotting overlays music cues on picture; CutTimeline provides the multi-track timeline with drift-nudge controls. scenes.ts and score.ts are read by two or more steps each, which is why they live here as shared fixtures rather than inside any one step directory. The Frames step has graduated to its own context; MotionShotLab has been removed as the VFX panel is not yet rebuilt.
contexts.name: production-phases

contexts.description: Step 1 of the production pipeline — a topic goes in, a structured notebook comes out. ResearchStep presents a two-section view (Topic for input and run control; Board for triage once a notebook exists) with a background-job model so the research run survives navigation. The beats/ sub-directory (BeatVariantBoard, ModeChooser, SlotColumn, VariantTile, beats.ts, useBeatPicks) extends the step with a beat-picking surface where users choose which research cards become script beats across trailer/free/educational discipline modes. The _parts/ directory contains the triage card tiles, follow-up queue, scope bar/gate, and topic panel; scope.ts, followup.ts, and useFollowUps.ts carry the business logic for creator-scoping decisions and follow-up interrogation.
contexts.name: research-step

contexts.description: Step 2 of the production pipeline — reads the Research notebook and outputs a scored, versioned screenplay. ScriptStep presents four tabs answering four distinct questions: Candidates (which render to use), Coverage (who used what card and for how long), Spend (how weight is distributed across one budget), and Tracks (running order bridging to the Frames step). The _notes/ directory manages the sticky notebook and recalibration controls; _matrix/ provides the four measurement surfaces; _parts/ carries BeatList, HypothesisColumn, Meters, ConstraintLedger, and GatePanel; recalibrate.ts enforces four contract guards discovered in UAT; the /api/recalibrate route drives a headless Claude Code process to turn accumulated notes into an edit plan.
contexts.name: script-step

contexts.description: The cross-step notebook module — the canonical data structure a research run produces and that all downstream steps (Script, Frames, Motion, Score, Cut) read from. types.ts defines Fact, Mechanism, Reversal, and the Notebook type; facts.ts, unknowns.ts, cards.ts, conclusions.ts, and dimensions.ts are the live fixture from the 2026-08-11 Bitcoin run used as real prototype content across all surfaces. NotebookBody.tsx and EvidenceLog.tsx are the read-surface components; sections/ (Apparatus, Argument, H, and the newly added Shared) break the notebook into structured sections — Shared.tsx extracts the CurrencyBody and SourcesBody markup that both NotebookBody and EvidenceLog previously duplicated; stepStore.ts provides the per-project IndexedDB key-value store.
contexts.name: shared-notebook

contexts.description: The Gravitone 'Obsidian' dark-cinematic design system. tokens.ts is the single source for all color literals, easing curves, surface classes, and motion presets; GravitoneTokens emits every --gt-* CSS variable server-side to prevent FOUC; globals.css defines the Signal Layer contract for audio-reactive visuals. Primitives.tsx, Equalizer.tsx, StudioFrame.tsx, and NotificationBell.tsx provide core atoms; Modal, Field, AuthGate, and UserMenu extend the library with interactive surface patterns; HarnessBridge.tsx injects the UAT test-automation overlay into the component tree so integration tests can observe and drive the live UI without a separate harness binary.
contexts.name: studio-design-system

contexts.description: The project management and studio routing layer. The landing page gates entry behind Google auth (GateContactSheet); /projects displays the production matrix shelf — a heat-grid of projects × six pipeline steps; /studio/[projectId] opens a named project on its active step via a horizontal Stepper rail. The studio route uses a dynamic segment so the project ID is URL-native, enabling direct linking to any step of any project. The /playground route provides a sandboxed component harness for UI experimentation outside the project flow.
contexts.name: studio-navigation

contexts.api_surface: internal lib only — consumed by /api/recalibrate, /api/frames, /api/foundry/extract routes
contexts.description: The server-side text/reasoning abstraction layer — one capability (reason) routed across two providers (claude-cli local subprocess, Google cloud API) with zero vendor coupling above lib/text/. router.ts builds a fallback chain from deployment posture and environment keys, walking from the preferred local binary to the cloud endpoint when the former is absent or fails; types.ts defines TextProvider, TextRequest, TextResult, TurnClass, and TextProvenance with the same vocabulary as the imaging layer; providers/claudeCli.ts and providers/google.ts are the two adapters; pricing.ts and log.ts mirror the imaging layer's cost-tracking and credential-scrubbing contracts. TurnClass (edit-plan, scene-direction, style-synthesis, probe) is the routing and spend-attribution key — an unlabelled call is a type error.
contexts.name: text-providers

contexts.description: The trailer discipline variant of Step 2 — turns research beats into a scored trailer cut with structural acts, energy curve, and withholding mechanics. TrailerScript is the root surface; StructurePanel and MovementSection organise acts and kinetic moves; EnergyCurve visualises intensity across the cut; PromiseLedger and WithholdingPanel model the audience-contract layer unique to trailers; BeatEditor, ConnectorPick, and RaisesChips handle per-beat editing and raises annotation; cut.ts and structure.ts carry the data model and scoring logic; useTrailerCut is the state hook; trailerFixtures.ts supplies a seeded demo cut for prototype sessions.
contexts.name: trailer-script
